links.note: Asks whether an original, intelligent person may do badly at school and whether that is failure - the giftedness-vs-school-rank question the architect answers in 31737 by naming classmates who always came first and are now in very ordinary jobs. The answer key's 'these people rise high' is that same claim. 31741 is the exercise heading that also contains the other two sub-parts; 31722 is the broader framing principle.
The definitional part - who counts as an 'unusual' learner - is stated only in 31741. No plot beat defines the term; 31736 merely describes his own subject-by-subject record.

What schools can do to draw out an unusual learner's best; the answer key ('encourage them to learn what they like best') is 31722's principle that each child differs in how they learn and in what interests them. 31735 (Mrs Gupta spotting his sketches) is one teacher's instance, not what the school should do.
